candidates.spoken: What If the Atlantic Ocean Current Shut Down?
Up to 25% of northern heat rides one current.
A shutdown wouldn't plunge Europe into an ice age.
Harsher northern European winters and shifted rain belts.
The Atlantic overturning circulation shut down.
But winters would harden, and rain belts would shift south.
Climate models say it will weaken this century.
It would not all happen at once.
So the danger isn't an ice age.
It keeps parts of Europe 4 to 10 °C warmer.

script.spoken: 25% of northward heat. Climate models say it will weaken this century. It keeps parts of Europe 4 to 10 °C warmer. Claims of a 15 to 20 °C crash are considered incorrect. But winters would harden, and rain belts would shift south. In Greenland's past, similar swings brought 8 to 15 °C within decades. So the danger isn't an ice age. It's speed.
